scores.strengths: Safest type decision of the three, and I verified every rule it claims is unaffected really is. Reusing COLLAPSED verbatim means zero edits to operand_ok (expression.py:144-162), _passthrough (175-183), _output_shape (186-196), _align_widths (kernels.py:122-143) and apply_cube's elementwise short-circuit (kernels.py:193-194) -- (A,B,1) against (A,B,M) broadcasts natively and _align_widths' `lead = max(shape[:-1], key=t[0]*t[1])` picks (A,B) correctly whenever any operand is non-constant. Its _pick form `if self.op_weight is None: return self._rng.choice(faces[self._rng.choice(sorted(faces))])` is literally generator.py:274, so the two _randbelow draws are preserved. Registry.daily_fields as a PARALLEL tuple (leaving registry.fields = the 8 minute fields, read at generator.py:78 and tokens.py:80) is the cleanest reason the search RNG cannot move. Only design that gets the mis-flagged set right: I measured in_sustain_mean/_stddev/_product are real-valued (they return nanmean / sqrt(var) / prod at dt_in.py:820-859) while in_sustain itself genuinely propagates a 0/1 mask (dt_in.py:863-877) and must stay flagged. Its load_plugins resetting catalog._DEFAULT = None is the only plugin mechanism of the three that cannot break a pytest session or its own tests. Alone catches the parser's self.daily_fields bool colliding with registry.daily_fields and renames it; alone refuses a bare `age` alias; alone raises the float32 / 1e12-cap precision trap.
scores.flaws: (1) Its headline "single non-obvious finding" is inverted. It writes: "An implementer who patches only the obvious _load_leaf_cube gets a working div(day_sum(Amt), FloatCap) and a hard failure on every factor built from daily leaves alone." I ran plan_rounds with a COLLAPSED stub leaf: div(day_sum(Amt), FloatCap) plans S[1] -> P[1] with the div node in MODE_P, so the turnover factor is precisely the one that raises `panel operand DF:FloatCap unavailable` without the _run_panel_round branch (engine.py:356-363). The expressions that exercise _load_leaf_cube are day_mean(mul(Ret, LimitWidth)), in_expand(FloatCap,241) and cross_mean(FloatCap,5) (all single S rounds). Its WP4 step ordering, its risk R1 and its test rationale ("a test suite built around the turnover example passes") all rest on the inverted version. (2) Its contract_hash mechanism is inert on the production store. It proposes `parts = {"meta_sha256": self.meta_sha256}; ...; self.contract_hash = canonical_hash(parts)` for "CubeStore ... SegmentedCubeStore(..., daily_root=None)". SegmentedCubeStore is NOT a subclass of CubeStore (MRO verified: (SegmentedCubeStore, object)), never calls super().__init__, has no self.meta_sha256, and sets contract_hash = canonical_hash(self.contract) from a 3-key dict at store.py:324-329. open_cube_store returns a SegmentedCubeStore for any compute root (store.py:401), i.e. the server store -- so the daily sha either AttributeErrors or never mixes in. It cites tests/test_store_layouts.py:50 as verification; that line is `assert seg.contract_hash != mono.contract_hash and len(seg.contract["segment_meta_sha256"]) == 2`, the segmented path its snippet does not fit. (3) "The report's generations then reflects what actually ran, which it already does (it is derived, not assumed)" is false: gp.py has `report.generations = n_gen`, assigned from the planned count, so its wall_seconds break over-reports. (4) It never names AlphaCube's own on-disk ExemplarCache: view_cache_key (rankban.py:242-249) hashes only dates[0]/dates[-1]/len(dates)/n_symbols/sample sizes and ExemplarCache stores fingerprints under root/<view_key>/ (rankban.py:157-180), so a rebuilt daily field silently reuses rank fingerprints for DF:-bearing expressions and the rank ban refuses the wrong candidates. It fixes Partura's PanelSet.view_id and misses this one. (5) "grows searchable(include_boolean=False) from 218 to 220 (measured)" -- I measured 218 -> 221 for its own set of three (214 -> 217 on the generator's actual default filter, which is include_resource_risk=False too). (6) Its synthetic daily planes are random lognormals, so an align-by-position bug in a symbol SUBSET is statistically invisible; store.view preserves the caller's symbol order (store.py:211) and sets _contiguous=False (store.py:419), so that case is reachable.

scores.strengths: Two unique catches that are both real. First: run_mining needs NO new parameter for the GP hooks, because pipeline.py:361 does `gp.update(gp_params or {})` and line 376 does `GPMiner(..., **gp)` -- and gp_params is not serialized into meta.json (pipeline.py:491 writes a fixed dict), so a Callable can ride there safely. That is strictly less plumbing than the other two. Second: banned_substructures is check_ban_key-validated on the GP path only (gp.py:250) and handed raw to BatchRewarder on the RL path (pipeline.py:408), so an RL run silently bans nothing on a malformed key. Its construction-time weight validation is aimed at a real crash: generate's fallback calls self._pick(self._root_ops_of("reduce")) and _pick would reach self._rng.choice(sorted({})) -> IndexError; I measured that pool at 26 specs today, so zeroing it is reachable. hook_rng is the right diagnosis of Partura's `G.accept(e, u=self._rng.random())` -- a hook drawing from the miner's RNG a data-dependent number of times makes the run unreproducible from its seed. Best fixture design of the three: identifiable values FloatCap[d,s] = 1e9*(s+1)+d on a non-square grid plus a non-ascending symbol subset is the only proposal that can actually catch position-vs-label alignment. Its per-call self._daily_t device cache is the only one that avoids re-materialising the (D,S) tensor once per consuming edge in a P round (engine.py:356's operand() checks Constant before values, so an uncached branch repeats the copy and the mask). Correctly documents the four live orientations and that a transpose yields a plausible panel, not a crash.
scores.flaws: (1) Its one genuinely novel idea does not do what it claims. The rule is "_passthrough: daily_only=all(s.daily_only for s in shapes)", but Constant._infer_shape returns WIDE_DEGENERATE (expression.py:137), whose new field defaults False -- so div(FloatCap, 2.0) comes out daily_only=False (all([True, False]) is False, measured), while its own test plan asserts "div(FloatCap, 2.0) True". The design's test would fail against the design's implementation. Worse, the new operand_ok rule `if spec.needs_full_m and operand.shape.daily_only: return False` then does not fire for day_sum(div(FloatCap, 2.0)) or day_sum(log(FloatCap)), so the legacy carve-out hole the fourth Shape field exists to close stays open for any daily expression touching a constant. (2) Its wall-clock code does not run: `report.stopped_early = "wall clock"; break` is placed inside the generation loop, but `report = self._commit()` only executes after the loop in gp.py's mine() -- UnboundLocalError. And unlike search-usability it never fixes `report.generations = n_gen`, so an early stop over-reports generations. (3) The registry latch breaks its own tests. op() raising once build_registry has returned is process-global with no reset, yet WP-H5's test is "real_valued=True on a throwaway @op whose kernel returns a constant" -- defined at test time, after default_registry() has been built by an earlier test in the same pytest process. Nothing in the design resets registry_closed. Its own R7 already concedes the latch will fire on real code. (4) It names only in_sustain_stddev as mis-flagged ("AlphaCube's own in_sustain_stddev"), so its stated AC break is 214 -> 215; measured, the correct set is three and the number is 214 -> 217, which reopens WP-H6 and every count it pins. (5) It puts the daily branch FIRST in parser.name() and includes a bare `age` alias, arguing "putting it first means a future name collision fails the disjointness test loudly" -- it does the opposite: first-position means a collision silently shadows an existing minute name (parser.py:133-143 resolves reg.fields then FIELD_ALIASES then DAILY_MACROS). (6) It deliberately declines to fix view_cache_key (its R11), so the ExemplarCache staleness ships behind an unenforced operational rule.

scores.strengths: The most accurate of the three against source -- every empirical claim I re-measured came out exactly as stated. Python 3.11.14, seed 7: choice -> [2,1,3] then random()=0.650934; choices(weights=[1]*5) -> [1,0,3] then 0.072436. Default generator vocabulary 214 specs, {dt:108, nd:46, nt:44, shared:16}. And it is the only design that states the engine-gap attribution correctly: "the common div(day_sum(Amt), FloatCap) turnover factor hits it immediately" (the panel gap) -- confirmed by running plan_rounds. Its make_scorer keeps BOTH built-in branches verbatim and first AND lets an unregistered kind fall through to the same PanelScorer(...) call at scoring.py:519, so the existing ValueError("kind must be ic or rank_ic, not ...") still comes out of the same place; the other two move or wrap that error. It is the only design that FIXES view_cache_key (daily=None, default byte-identical), which is the real on-disk staleness (ExemplarCache keys on it, rankban.py:170-180). It alone catches that self.cost_per_side is assigned after the `if self._rich:` block (gp.py:320 uses the local float(cost_per_side), the attribute lands ~9 lines later), so a context builder must use the local. It alone sets report.generations = done_gen. Its four-attribute duck-type check on a registered scorer at construction maps exactly onto the four real sites: target_t64/target_ranks_t (gp.py:325-326), score_combined (env.py:284), columns (gp.py:876). leaf_slots is the only proposal that addresses the positional problem: _operand_reqs gives an nd-face binary a "daily" requirement in BOTH slots (generator.py:323-324), so without a positional hint the search cannot know operand 1 of cs_bucket_rank is the key -- i.e. it is the only design that makes "rank y inside its own cap decile" something the search DRAWS rather than merely parses. Its R5 is a test-validity trap the others miss: the conftest store is n_symbols=10 (tests/conftest.py:17), so a cs_bucket_* decile test on it asserts all-NaN == all-NaN. DailyFieldView.__getitem__ makes the leaf layer and the reward layer read one object.
scores.flaws: (1) Its operand_ok claim is overstated. The overview says "day_*/in_*/nt_* reject the daily leaf in ALL modes, legacy included" and "I made that rejection total", but the code adds only `and not isinstance(operand, DailyFeature)` to the non-strict branch -- which blocks a BARE leaf, not day_sum(log(FloatCap)) or day_sum(div(FloatCap, 2.0)), both of which stay legal under parse_legacy and evaluate as a width-1 identity through apply_cube's compute_axis=="M" path. Its test set (day_sum(FloatCap), in_mean(FloatCap,5), nt_cs_rank(FloatCap)) is all bare leaves, so the tests pass while the claim is false. Note in_mean/nt_cs_rank were already rejected in both modes (measured: operand_ok is False strict and legacy, because neither reduces_m), so only day_* was ever at issue. (2) It pins the wrong number. AC-11's gate is `len(searchable(include_boolean=False, include_resource_risk=False)) == 216` "with a comment naming the two kernels", and it says "The fact map named one kernel; there are two." Measured: in_sustain_product is mis-flagged on the identical mechanism, so the true value is 217, and the pinned test fails the moment anyone fixes the third kernel. (3) Largest new API surface, and most of it is unnecessary: run_mining gains seven parameters (daily_store, daily_leaves, steering, steering_arm, steering_options, fitness_options, max_seconds) where typed-correctness demonstrates the GP hooks can ride in the already-spread gp_params (pipeline.py:361/376). More defaults crossing pipeline -> GPMiner -> TypedTreeGenerator is more places for one to be dropped, and Steering carries a Callable so nothing about the intervention is recoverable from meta.json beyond a hand-written note (its own R11). (4) The --plugin pre-parse off a copy of sys.argv so `choices=scorer_kinds()` can be accurate is the most fragile CLI mechanism of the three; its own R8 concedes a failed plugin import surfaces as an argparse "invalid choice" on --fitness. Its load_plugins guard (`if specs and catalog._DEFAULT is not None: raise`) is also order-sensitive inside a pytest session, where an earlier test will have built the default registry -- minimal-diff's reset is more robust. (5) `_nan` in its _run_panel_round snippet is undefined.

graft: From typed-correctness: route the GP hooks through gp_params instead of new run_mining parameters. pipeline.py:361 already does `gp.update(gp_params or {})` and line 376 `GPMiner(..., **gp)`, and gp_params is never serialized (pipeline.py:491 writes a fixed dict), so op_weights / accept / mutation_checks_bans / max_seconds need zero signature changes. Delete `steering`, `steering_arm`, `steering_options`, `fitness_options` and `max_seconds` from search-usability's run_mining signature and keep only `daily_store` and `daily_leaves` (those genuinely have to reach open_cube_store and CubeEngine before GPMiner exists).

From typed-correctness: validate the weight table at TypedTreeGenerator.__init__, specifically that `[s for s in self.specs if s.reduces_m and not s.non_root]` stays non-empty after dropping weight-0 operators. I measured that pool at 26 specs; emptying it makes generate()'s fallback reach `self._rng.choice(sorted({}))` -> IndexError, and _gen("daily", 1, ...) raise ShapeError forever. Also validate: every key names a registered operator, every value a finite float >= 0, and the accept hook is callable with exactly one positional parameter.

From typed-correctness: expose `gen.hook_rng = random.Random((seed * 2654435761) & 0xFFFFFFFF)` and document that an accept hook must draw from it, never from gen._rng. Partura's current hook does `G.accept(e, u=self._rng.random())`, which makes the trajectory depend on how many candidates were thinned. This is a precondition for search-usability's own `--arm both` comparison meaning anything.

From typed-correctness: the identifiable-value fixture. Write the synthetic daily planes as FloatCap[d,s] = 1e9*(s+1) + d on a non-square grid, and test a symbol subset in NON-ASCENDING order (store.view(symbols=[s3,s0,s7]) preserves the caller's order at store.py:211 and sets _contiguous=False at store.py:419, so the fancy-index path is reachable). search-usability's DailyFieldView builds _rows/_cols by label, which is correct, but random-valued planes cannot prove it.

From typed-correctness: the explicit shape assertion in _load_leaf_cube -- `want = (hi-lo, view.n_days) if mode == MODE_S else (view.n_symbols, hi-lo)`, raise if arr.shape != want, before the unsqueeze(-1). This is the one place a lo:hi slip produces a silently wrong chunk rather than an error, and it is what makes the chunk-invariance test diagnosable instead of just red.

From typed-correctness: the per-evaluate device cache for the P-round daily tensor (self._daily_t, allocated in evaluate() and cleared in its existing finally at engine.py:199-204). engine.py:356's operand() tests isinstance(c.expr, Constant) BEFORE consulting `values`, so an uncached DailyFeature branch re-does the numpy->torch copy and the mask once per consuming edge.

From typed-correctness: validate gp_params['banned_substructures'] with check_ban_key in run_mining so BOTH branches get it. Today only the GP path validates (gp.py:250); pipeline.py:408 hands the tuple raw to BatchRewarder, so a malformed key on an RL run bans nothing, silently.

From minimal-diff: rename the parser's boolean `self.daily_fields` (parser.py:136, 146, 147, 151) to `coerce_bare_fields`. search-usability keeps the bool AND introduces reg.daily_fields, so two unrelated things read as the same name in one function.

From minimal-diff: have load_plugins reset `catalog._DEFAULT = None` after loading rather than raising when it is already built. search-usability's guard is order-sensitive inside a pytest session (an earlier test will have built the default registry) and would fail its own positive plugin test; the reset is what Partura's install() does today and it works. Keep minimal-diff's R8 caveat in the docstring: a library caller holding an already-returned Registry object still sees a short vocabulary.

From minimal-diff: drop `choices=` from --fitness (cli.py:330) and validate inside cmd_mine against scorer_kinds(), instead of pre-parsing --plugin out of sys.argv to keep argparse's choices accurate. Losing shell completion on one flag is cheaper than the failure mode search-usability's own R8 describes.

From minimal-diff: the correct mis-flagged set and numbers -- in_sustain_mean, in_sustain_stddev, in_sustain_product, giving searchable(include_boolean=False) 218 -> 221 and the generator's default (include_resource_risk=False too) 214 -> 217. in_sustain itself genuinely returns a 0/1 propagation mask (dt_in.py:863-877) and must stay flagged.

From minimal-diff: the float32 warning for 1e12-yuan caps, and store a log(FloatCap) plane alongside the raw one. Ratios and ranks are unaffected (~6e-8 relative) but ts_delta(FloatCap, 1) differences two nearly equal large numbers; the engine only widens to float64 in dtype="float64" reference mode.
must_fix: generate()'s fallback bypasses acceptable() entirely, so the accept hook (and the ban set) is void exactly when it bites hardest. generator.py:118-125: after max_retries*4 = 64 failed attempts, `return self._collapse_leaf(self._pick(self._root_ops_of("reduce")))` -- no acceptable() call. I proved it: with a generator whose acceptable() returns False for everything, generate() still returns `day_open(Ret)` after 64 rejections, and generate_population(8) returns 8 unaccepted depth-2 day_*(Feature) trees. GPMiner._mutate routes mutation exhaustion into the same call (gp.py:668). ALL THREE designs claim the hook is consulted at every acceptance point and enumerate five or seven sites (minimal-diff: 'generate, mutate_subtree, mutate_operator, mutate_hoist and crossover for free'; typed-correctness: 'every existing call site is covered for free'; search-usability: 'test_accept_hook_is_called_at_every_acceptance_point'); none includes this one. For Partura this is the difference between a steer arm and a control arm -- the tighter the guidance, the larger the fraction of the population that is un-steered minimal trees, which is the most likely explanation for a steer/control comparison looking like noise. Fix: gate the fallback (re-draw under the hook with a bounded retry, or raise a named error naming the hook) and ship it in the SAME commit as the hook, with a test that an always-False hook yields no tree rather than an unaccepted one.

board_limit's board rules are silently symbol-format-dependent, and this repo contains both formats -- so all three designs' claim that LimitWidth and BoardCode are 'derived, exact, need no build step and are testable on the synthetic cube' is wrong on the default fixture. tradability.py:23-25 tests s.startswith(('688','689')) / ('300','301','302') / ('4','8','92'). tests/test_tradability.py:11 uses '600000.SH'; synthetic.py:78 (and therefore tests/conftest.py) uses f'SH.6{i:05d}'. Measured: on the prefix format every rule misses and board_limit returns a uniform 0.10 plane. So (a) minimal-diff's test 'derive("LimitWidth",...) equals board_limit(symbols,dates).T exactly, including the 20200824 GEM switch and the 688/300/4-8-92 prefixes' compares two constant planes on the conftest store and asserts nothing about any prefix; and (b) if the production store uses the prefix format, LimitWidth ships as a constant and BoardCode as a single category, at 100% finite coverage, so no coverage floor catches it. Fix: assert in derive() that at least one non-default board rule fires (else raise, naming the first few symbols), change the synthetic fixture to a format on which the rules do fire, and check the server store's actual symbol format before the build runs.

ExemplarCache has no data identity, and only search-usability fixes it. view_cache_key (rankban.py:242-249) hashes dates[0], dates[-1], len(dates), n_symbols and the two sample sizes -- no store identity at all -- and ExemplarCache stores rank fingerprints on disk under root/<view_key>/, deleting other view keys on construction (rankban.py:157-187). A DF:-bearing expression's fingerprint therefore survives a daily-field rebuild and a switch between two daily roots, and the symptom is a rank-similarity ban that refuses candidates it should not, not a crash. Mix the daily store's fingerprint into view_cache_key with a default that keeps the current string byte-identical. Do not rely on contract_hash for this (see the next item), and do not leave it as an operational 'run clean_exemplar_cache.py' rule (typed-correctness R11).

If contract_hash is used as the daily-data identity, it must be changed in SegmentedCubeStore, not just CubeStore. SegmentedCubeStore is not a subclass of CubeStore (MRO: (SegmentedCubeStore, object)), never calls super().__init__, has no self.meta_sha256, and sets contract_hash = canonical_hash(self.contract) from {base_minute_meta_sha256, index_sha256, segment_meta_sha256} at store.py:324-329. open_cube_store returns a SegmentedCubeStore for any compute root (store.py:401), which is what the server uses. minimal-diff's snippet targets CubeStore's one-key dict only, so on production it either raises AttributeError or silently never mixes the daily sha in.

The mis-flagged kernel set is exactly three, and the vocabulary numbers are 218 -> 221 (include_boolean=False) and 214 -> 217 (the generator's actual default, which is include_resource_risk=False as well). I measured each step: clearing in_sustain_stddev alone gives 219/215, adding in_sustain_mean gives 220/216, adding in_sustain_product gives 221/217. in_sustain must stay flagged -- it genuinely propagates a 0/1 mask (dt_in.py:863-877). typed-correctness names one kernel, search-usability two (and pins ==216 as an acceptance test), minimal-diff names the right three but states the two-kernel number. Whoever lands this must pin 217 and must re-pin tests/test_planted_signal.py's seed, because the draw sequence shifts from generation 1 and that test asserts best_fitness > 0.2 at seed=7.

report.generations must come from the loop counter, not n_gen, and stopped_early must be set on a local applied after _commit(). gp.py assigns `report.generations = n_gen` (the planned count) after the loop, and `report = self._commit()` only exists after the loop -- so minimal-diff's wall_seconds break over-reports generations and typed-correctness's in-loop `report.stopped_early = "wall clock"` is an UnboundLocalError. search-usability's `report.generations = done_gen` is the correct form; adopt it.

The daily-field branch in parser.name() must come AFTER the minute-field/alias branch, must not include a bare `age` alias, and must be covered by a disjointness test. parser.name() (parser.py:133-143) resolves reg.fields, then FIELD_ALIASES, then DAILY_MACROS, then DAILY_NAME_ALIASES. typed-correctness puts the daily branch first and adds `"age": "ListedDays"`; first position means any future collision silently shadows an existing minute name rather than erroring, which is the opposite of what it argues. I checked all three alias sets against CUBE_FIELDS, FIELD_ALIASES, DAILY_MACROS, DAILY_NAME_ALIASES and every registered operator name: no collisions today, so the only exposure is future drift -- which is exactly what the ordering plus a disjointness test closes.

day_* over a daily-derived COLLAPSED expression stays legal under parse_legacy in every design, and no design's tests cover it. minimal-diff deliberately leaves operand_ok untouched; search-usability blocks only `isinstance(operand, DailyFeature)`; typed-correctness's daily_only=all(...) is False as soon as a Constant is involved (Constant's shape is WIDE_DEGENERATE, expression.py:137). So day_sum(log(FloatCap)) and day_sum(div(FloatCap, 2.0)) parse under legacy and evaluate as a width-1 identity through apply_cube's compute_axis=='M' path. Decide this once and test the DERIVED case, not just the bare leaf: either propagate the daily property with any() over operands (and accept that it newly rejects some legacy trees over mixed collapsed subtrees), or pin the identity behaviour explicitly so a later change to the width-1 carve-out cannot silently change what a daily leaf means.
